s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive lower limb weakness with fluctuating course and spinal involvement
salient_findings: Fluctuating lower-limb weakness
Ascending spastic weakness of the lower limbs
Urinary retention and constipation
Increased tone and preserved bulk in the lower limbs
Posterior epidural mass from D5 to D7
key_facts: 18-year-old man
6 months of fluctuating lower-limb weakness
Awoke one morning unable to move his legs but recovered movement over 30 minutes
Remained asymptomatic for 4 months
Developed ascending spastic weakness of the lower limbs over 3 months
Unable to stand
Urinary retention requiring a Foley catheter
One month of constipation
Denied trauma, fever, steroid or other drug intake, and infections
Non-obese with BMI 23.3 kg/m2
No signs of Cushing syndrome or endocrinopathy
Increased tone and preserved bulk in the lower limbs
Medical Research Council grade 3/5 at hips and knees and 0/5 at ankles and toes
Brisk knee and ankle jerks
Bilateral extensor plantar responses
Graded sensory loss below the D10 level
Normal routine hematological and biochemical tests
Normal cerebrospinal fluid analysis
Unremarkable plain radiographs of the spine
Magnetic resonance imaging of the thoracic spine demonstrated a posterior epidural mass from D5 to D7

shortlist.label: Spinal epidural lipomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Posterior epidural mass with homogeneous hyperintensity on MRI, suggestive of fat

shortlist.label: Spinal cord tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive lower limb weakness with spinal involvement and mass on MRI

shortlist.label: Ependymoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible intramedullary spinal cord tumor given graded sensory loss and motor weakness

shortlist.label: Spinal epidural abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Although denied infections, possibility of abscess cannot be entirely ruled out without further testing

shortlist.label: Intramedullary spinal cord tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Fluctuating course and progressive weakness suggest a possible tumor within the spinal cord

raw.rationale: The presence of a posterior epidural mass from D5 to D7 that is homogeneously hyperintense on both T1-weighted and T2-weighted MRI sequences, suggestive of fat, supports this diagnosis. The patient's symptoms of fluctuating lower-limb weakness, ascending spastic weakness, and graded sensory loss are consistent with spinal cord compression by the epidural mass.

rejected.label: Spinal cord tumor
rejected.why: The MRI description of the mass as hyperintense on both T1-weighted and T2-weighted sequences, suggestive of fat, does not support a tumor diagnosis.

rejected.label: Ependymoma
rejected.why: Ependymomas are typically intramedullary tumors and would not be described as epidural masses on MRI.

rejected.label: Spinal epidural abscess
rejected.why: The patient denied fever and infections, and the cerebrospinal fluid analysis was normal, making an abscess less likely. Additionally, the MRI description does not suggest an abscess.

rejected.label: Intramedullary spinal cord tumor
rejected.why: The mass is described as epidural, not intramedullary, on MRI, which does not support this diagnosis.
